title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
why_read: A memory architecture for multimodal AI agents that claims big efficiency gains, relevant to anyone building long-running AI assistants.
analysis: This paper tackles the problem of giving multimodal AI agents, ones that handle text and images together, useful long-term memory of past interactions. Instead of relying only on semantic similarity search over compressed summaries, it builds a graph connecting related memory episodes and lets the system pick different forms of evidence (summaries, captions, raw images) depending on the query. A trainable selector decides what level of detail is needed for each retrieved memory, which the authors say cuts token usage by about 90% compared to competing systems while improving results. This matters for anyone building production agent systems where context window and cost are real constraints.
